summary: Twelve concrete, comment-endorsed tools, resources, media picks, and games surfaced from a complete HN front-page comment crawl.
telegram_footer: 12 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Tailscale
items.source_story_title: New Mac Studio with M5 Max and M5 Ultra
items.summary: A mesh VPN that makes remote Mac screen sharing simple.
items.why_included: A hands-on user said its free tier worked great for remote Mac access.
items.evidence: The commenter uses Tailscale with macOS Screen Sharing between home and work Macs.

evidence_sources.author: lo_fye
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using the free version of TailScale to use macOS's built-in screen sharing app to use my home Mac mini from my work MacBook Pro. Works great!

items.name: Audiobookshelf
items.source_story_title: Bookshelf – Self-hosted eBook library that runs on object storage
items.summary: A self-hosted server for audiobooks, podcasts, and ebooks.
items.why_included: A regular user praised its broader-than-expected media support.
items.evidence: The commenter uses Audiobookshelf for podcasts, audiobooks, and ebooks and called it great.

evidence_sources.author: BloodyIron
evidence_sources.excerpt: I'm a fan of audiobookshelf. Don't let the name fool you, it does a lot! I use it for podcasts, audio books, & ebooks. It's great!

items.name: Middlemak
items.summary: A keyboard layout that reduces finger travel while retaining QWERTY familiarity.
items.why_included: A developer preferred it over Workman and Colemak for daily coding.
items.evidence: The commenter found Middlemak minimized finger travel and awkward motions without discarding much QWERTY muscle memory.

evidence_sources.author: tpmoney
evidence_sources.excerpt: I tried a couple different layouts and landed on something called "middlemak"[1]. Of all the ones I tried, it really felt like the one with the least overall finger travel and awkward things to type in my day to day software development work

items.name: Easyboot
items.source_story_title: Show HN: I wrote a BASIC interpreter that boots on UEFI machines
items.summary: A dependency-free boot manager and bootable disk-image creator.
items.why_included: A commenter directly recommended it as a possible GRUB or rEFIt replacement.
items.evidence: The recommendation pointed to Easyboot in response to a request for an alternative boot manager.

items.name: ImHex
items.summary: A graphical hex editor for inspecting, decoding, and visualizing binary data.
items.why_included: A hands-on user reported good results using it for binary visualization.
items.evidence: The commenter uses ImHex for the same binary-inspection purpose discussed in the thread.

evidence_sources.author: pdpi
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using ImHex[0] for this purpose, to pretty good effect.

items.name: You Don’t Need Animations
items.source_story_title: Tooltips need a delay, and then they need to skip it
items.summary: A UI essay on where motion helps and where restraint works better.
items.why_included: A commenter called the whole post worth reading and memorable.
items.evidence: The commenter connected its final example to tooltip behavior and said the detail stayed with them.

evidence_sources.author: brixie
evidence_sources.excerpt: that whole post is worth a read, I think, if you found this interesting

items.name: Dolly Parton’s America
items.summary: A podcast series exploring Dolly Parton’s life, work, and cultural reach.
items.why_included: A listener highly recommended its unusually rich one-on-one access.
items.evidence: The commenter said the podcast helped explain why people loved Dolly Parton and called it fantastic.

evidence_sources.author: mattsolle
evidence_sources.excerpt: I highly recommend it. Does a great job interviewing Dolly

items.name: Other Minds: The Octopus, the Sea, and the Deep Origins of Consciousness
items.source_story_title: Octopus intelligence may be related to never-before-seen mutation
items.summary: Peter Godfrey-Smith’s book on cephalopod minds and the evolution of consciousness.
items.why_included: Two commenters independently praised it as excellent and a great deeper read.
items.evidence: Commenters endorsed the book as an excellent route into octopus intelligence and consciousness.

evidence_sources.author: adolph
evidence_sources.excerpt: Godfrey-Smith is the author of "Other Minds: The Octopus, the Sea, and the Deep Origins of Consciousness," which is a great read to delve further.

evidence_sources.author: bookofjoe
evidence_sources.excerpt: Other Minds: The Octopus, the Sea, and the Deep Origins of Consciousness [excellent]

items.name: Artle
items.summary: An independent art game inspired by Wordle and designed for daily play.
items.why_included: Its creator said they still play it daily with their father.
items.evidence: The creator described Artle as a Wordle-inspired art game with lasting daily appeal.

evidence_sources.author: steinvakt2
evidence_sources.excerpt: I made an art game inspired by wordle some years ago. My dad and I still play it daily.

items.name: Iris
items.source_story_title: Nostr is an inclusive communication commons
items.summary: A fast web client for trying the decentralized Nostr social network.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended it as an easy first step into Nostr.
items.evidence: The commenter called Iris a great way for newcomers to get started with Nostr.

evidence_sources.author: donpdonp
evidence_sources.excerpt: for those simply looking to try nostr for the first time, https://iris.to is a great way to get started.

items.name: BuyVM
items.summary: A low-cost VPS provider offering KVM servers suitable for BSD.
items.why_included: A former BSD customer reported no issues and responsive support.
items.evidence: The commenter used BuyVM for BSD and found its support quick and helpful.

evidence_sources.author: SoftTalker
evidence_sources.excerpt: I used buyvm.net for BSD a while back. Didn't have any issues, and the few times I contacted their support they were quick to respond and helpful.

items.name: Roman Zolotarev’s OpenBSD Notes
items.summary: A compact collection of practical OpenBSD setup and operations notes.
items.why_included: An OpenBSD reader called the resource their go-to reference.
items.evidence: The commenter singled out Roman Zolotarev’s BSD notes as a frequently used resource.
